decisions.executionNote: Raise and orient the right gripper with elbow-up continuity, approaching the shifted basket; left arm stays parked.
Translate above the basket while pitching the open right gripper toward the rear egg. Maintain clearance before descent.
Approach the rear basket egg with an open gripper, adapting the grasp position to the live basket shift.
Adjust jaw alignment above the rear egg before final descent; the adjacent eggs remain close.
Lower and center over the rear egg, keeping the jaws open and the basket rim clear.
Close around the rear egg and lift slowly to check retention in the wrist view.
The egg was not retained. Reopen and move forward/down toward its new position in the basket.
Set the fingers slightly deeper around the centered egg, close fully, then lift to check the grasp.
The egg appears between the fingers. Lift clear of the basket and begin the transfer toward the holder, keeping the gripper closed.
Carry the retained egg toward the holder at clearance height and rotate into the placement approach.
Lower the held egg toward the rear-right holder cup; keep it closed until seated alignment is visible.
Seat and release the first egg into the rear-right cup, then lift slightly to inspect the placement.
First egg is visibly seated. Withdraw above the holder and move toward the basket for the next egg.
Approach the leftmost remaining basket egg with open jaws, finishing the downward grasp orientation.
Descend around the leftmost egg while watching clearance from the two adjacent eggs and basket rim.
Close on the centered second egg and lift vertically; confirm it remains between the jaws before transfer.
Lift the second egg clear and carry it toward the front-right cup with the gripper kept fully closed.
The second egg is no longer between the jaws. Return above the basket with open fingers to reacquire it more deeply.
Align lower over the leftmost remaining egg, correcting left and forward while keeping the gripper open.
Correct slightly inward from the basket rim, narrow the fingers around the left egg, and make a short retention-test lift.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed to verify the egg clears the basket and stays captured.
The egg remained in the basket. Reopen, center farther forward, and descend deeper so the fingers can surround its middle.
Center the left egg between the jaws, narrowing to avoid the rim, then close at a deeper grasp height.
Make a slow vertical retention test with the jaws closed; do not begin transfer until the egg clearly lifts.
The egg is still in the basket. Shift the open gripper forward and deeper to bring its fingers around the egg center instead of above it.
The rim is limiting descent. Raise slightly and pitch the fingers nearly vertical to approach the egg without catching the rim.
Align the near-vertical fingers around the egg's middle, close, and perform another short lift.
Reposition the open, near-vertical jaws farther over the egg rather than closing at its near edge.
The egg is now centered in the open jaws. Descend around its sides, close fully, and test a small lift.
The egg slipped forward during closure. Reopen and move the vertical jaws toward its near-side position before descending again.
The egg is now aligned with the finger pads. Close at this centered position and lift slowly to verify capture.
The fingers closed above the egg. Descend with the jaws open to bring the pads lower along its sides, monitoring rim contact.
Close gently from the lower centered position and make a short lift, checking whether the egg follows the pads.
Lift the apparently captured egg straight above the rim without rotating, keeping the jaws fully closed.
The egg is visibly retained above the basket. Carry it toward the front-right cup, maintaining a closed grip and clearance.
Lower the retained egg toward the front-right cup, leaving the jaws closed until alignment and seating can be checked.
Correct the egg inward over the front-right cup and lower a little more, using the cup rim in the wrist view.
Release the second egg into the front-right cup and withdraw upward to verify it stays seated.
Two eggs are visibly seated. Return above the two remaining basket eggs with the successful near-vertical grasp orientation.
Center the nearer remaining egg between the open jaws while descending toward the successful grasp height.
Narrow the jaws clear of the adjacent egg, center on the nearer egg, and close lower around its sides before a short lift.
The nearer egg moved left during closure. Recenter the open jaws over its new position, keeping clear of the rim.
Recenter on the nearer egg and lower the pads around its middle before closing; no transfer until retention is visible.
Lift straight away from the rim with the grip closed and inspect whether the third egg follows.
The egg was not retained. Reopen and approach deeper with the previously successful downward jaw orientation, avoiding premature closure.
Narrow to clear the basket rim, lower the pads slightly deeper around the centered egg, then close and make a small retention test.
Lift vertically with the jaws fully closed to verify the centered egg stays captured above the rim.
The third egg was not retained. Reopen and place the pads deeper, slightly nearer the robot, to surround rather than pinch above the egg.
Descent is contact-limited. Center slightly left, close without pushing lower, then lift gently to check retention.
Continue lifting the egg straight above the basket with the grip closed, checking that it remains fixed between the pads.
The egg slipped inward. Approach its new, more accessible position with open jaws and restore the successful downward orientation.
Descend around the egg now away from the rim, center the finger pads on its middle, then close and test a small lift.
Lift the centered egg straight above the basket, maintaining a fully closed gripper and checking retention before transfer.
Third egg is visibly held above the basket. Transfer it toward the empty left column of the holder, keeping the right wrist on its side.
Lower toward the rear-left cup and yaw the gripper to reach it while keeping the right wrist near the centerline.
Lower the third egg into the rear-left cup, release it, and lift the open fingers to inspect seating.
The third egg is seated. Withdraw from the holder and return above the basket for the final egg with the downward grasp orientation.
Move above the last egg and descend with open jaws, adapting to its position on the far-right side of the basket.
Align the final egg centrally under the open finger pads while descending, keeping the basket rim in view.
Back away from rim contact and begin yawing the open jaws to grasp the final egg across its shorter dimension.
Finish turning the jaws across the egg's short axis and approach from above with clearance from the basket wall.
Descend the rotated open jaws around the final egg's short sides, with a small lateral centering correction.
Close around the centered final egg without forcing the rim, then lift slowly to test retention.
The final egg was not retained. Reopen and lower the pads farther around its sides, shifting slightly inward from the wall.
Recenter the finger pads over the egg's nearer half, then close and make a short test lift without forcing deeper contact.
Lift slowly straight above the basket with the gripper closed, checking whether the final egg remains between the pads.
The last egg is visibly retained and the basket is empty. Carry it toward the empty front-left cup with the gripper closed.
The final egg slipped back into the basket during transfer. Return above its new left-side position and prepare a deeper grasp.
Approach the last egg now near the basket center with open fingers, correcting its image offset before the final grasp.
Lower the pads around the centered last egg, close fully, and make a short vertical retention test.
